Or the diff I output was computed from the old last_transition because the ACTION7 transition was appended but last_transition points to it… I'm confused. Let me re-verify: in this snippet, I first output the nodes (showing node 23 as 'p' px 9 — the player is now purple), then called ACTION7, then output the diff of last_transition. The diff shows the cross→purple change. If last_transition were the ACTION7 one, before_frame should already have the purple player (since the player turned purple in the previous MOUSE action), and after_frame should be identical → empty diff. So the diff showing the cross→purple change means last_transition is still the MOUSE(53,10) transition. So maybe transitions/last_transition only updates when board_changed=True? But the earlier MOUSE click (timer only) did produce a transition with a 2-cell diff… those had board_changed=True (the timer is part of the board).
OK, so the rule is: last_action_result and last_transition update on every action, but if ACTION7 didn't change the board, maybe the "transition" is recorded with before==after… in which case the diff should be empty. So the current state: the player is a 3×3 purple square at (52-54, 9-11). The purple square in the lower left is gone. The blue ball is intact. The purple square in the upper center of the HUD is also intact.
Hmm wait, actually let me reconsider what happened. Maybe clicking the player didn't "collect" the purple square. Maybe it was a "color swap": the player's white was swapped with… no, the square in the lower left turned black, not white.
Another interpretation: this is a "Simon" style or "match" game: the purple square in the lower left is the "goal" that the player should reach, and clicking the player teleports the player… no, the player didn't move.

Or: the game is "the player moves to the clicked position" — no, the player didn't move.
Wait, maybe I should reconsider: the purple square in the lower left wasn't a token but the "home base," and clicking the player made the player "return home"… but the player stayed at (53,10).
Let me look at the image once more: the player is now a purple 3×3 square at (52-54, 9-11), sitting on the dashed line. The dashed line continues from (51,12) up to the ball, and from (55,8), (57,6) down to where the purple square used to be.

The goal might be to move the player along the path to the blue ball. How to move? Maybe clicking a dot on the line moves the player one step toward that dot? Earlier, clicking (30,20) (an empty cell, not on the line) did nothing. The dots are at (51,12), (55,8), etc. Let me try clicking the dot at (51,12) (the next dot toward the ball) and see if the player moves.
Actually wait — maybe the player moves toward the clicked cell one step at a time per click. Earlier, clicking (14,48) — the direction from the player (53,10) to (14,48) is upper-right; the player should have moved to (52,11) or (51,12)… it didn't move. So no.

    return [(r,c,b[r][c],a[r][c]) for r in range(len(b)) for c in range(len(b[r])) if b[r][c]!=a[r][c]]
ch = diff(last_transition)
